verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT) Friday, April 10, off the coast of San Diego." (R1); "Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego" (R2); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 5:07 p.m. local time Friday" (R3); "SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact date, time, location, and safe splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "10-day moon mission" (R2); "10-day mission" (R3); "approximate 10-day mission" (R4); "historic 10-day mission" (R6); "record-breaking 10-day mission" (R7); "10-day flight" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe the mission as a 10-day mission, aligning with launch on April 1 and splashdown on April 10.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft began its final descent at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the spacecraft will enter ... at 7:53 p.m." (R1); "7:53 p.m.: When Orion reaches 400,000 feet ... first contact with the upper atmosphere" (R2); "7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere 400,000 feet" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Entry interface at 7:53 p.m. EDT is explicitly described as the start of descent into the atmosphere.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft endured a six-minute communications blackout due to extreme heat.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "planned six‑minute communications blackout ... as plasma forms around the capsule during peak heating" (R1); "planned six-minute communications blackout as plasma builds around the capsule" (R2); "six-minute communication blackout" during reentry (R3); "planned communications blackout expected to last about six minutes as plasma built" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state a planned six-minute blackout due to plasma from atmospheric heating.

verifications.claim: Artemis II reached Entry Interface at 400,000 feet at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "As Orion descends through about 400,000 feet ... at 7:53 p.m." (R1); "7:53 p.m.: When Orion reaches 400,000 feet" (R2); "7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere 400,000 feet" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Exact details of entry interface at 400,000 feet and 7:53 p.m. EDT match precisely.

verifications.claim: The communication blackout began at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "enter a planned six‑minute communications blackout at 7:53 p.m." (R1); "7:53 p.m. ... the start of a planned six-minute communications blackout" (R2); "7:53 p.m. ... begins its guided descent. Shortly after, Orion is in a planned communications blackout" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state blackout begins at entry interface, 7:53 p.m. EDT.

verifications.claim: Artemis II experienced peak heating or maximum plasma at approximately 5,000°F at 7:59 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "plasma forms around the capsule during peak heating" during blackout starting 7:53 p.m. (R1); "plasma builds around the capsule" at 7:53 p.m. (R2); "temperature around the heat shield will peak at around 5,000 Fahrenheit" during blackout from 7:53 p.m. (R3); "peak heating ... Temperatures can be up to 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit" ~1:20 after 7:53 p.m. (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Peak heating and ~5,000°F during blackout (7:53-~7:59 p.m.) supported, but exact time of 7:59 p.m. not specified; blackout ends around then.

verifications.claim: Drogue parachutes deployed at 8:03 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "deploy its drogue parachutes near 22,000 feet at 8:03 p.m." (R1); "8:03 p.m.: Around 22,000 feet ... the drogue parachutes will deploy" (R2); "8:03 p.m. At 23,400 feet, the drogue parachutes on Orion deployed" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and event directly confirmed.

verifications.claim: Main parachutes deployed at 8:04 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "unfurl its three main parachutes around 6,000 feet at 8:04 p.m." (R1); "8:04 p.m.: ... the three main parachutes will deploy" (R2); "8:04 p.m. At 5,400 feet, Orion’s drogue parachutes were cut and the three main parachutes deployed" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and event directly confirmed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II journey set a new record for human distance from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "traveling further into space than any humans have gone before"; "farthest any humans have been" (R3); "set a new record for human spaceflight" (R6); "new record for the farthest distance from Earth any humans have ever traveled" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it set a record for farthest human distance from Earth.
